source: Round 5 plumbing deep-dive (IPC 2021 tables/sizing, UPC differences labeled UPC) by plumb5

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 608.1 (ICC PMG CodeNotes: Backflow Preventers, 2021 IPC/IRC, iccsafe.org)
facts.fact: In IPC 2021 Table 608.1, reduced pressure principle assemblies (ASSE 1013) and double check assemblies (ASSE 1015) are listed in sizes 3/8 in through 16 in. Pressure vacuum breakers (ASSE 1020) and spill-resistant vacuum breakers (ASSE 1056) are listed only in sizes 1/2 in through 2 in.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 608.1 (ICC PMG CodeNotes: Backflow Preventers, 2021)
facts.fact: A spill-resistant vacuum breaker (SVB, ASSE 1056) is rated for high or low hazard but protects against backsiphonage only, the same rating as a pressure vacuum breaker. Unlike a PVB, it is designed not to spit water from its vent when it is pressurized.
facts.note: The no-spill design is the purpose of the ASSE 1056 device; the table itself lists hazard and backflow type.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 608.1 (ICC PMG CodeNotes: Backflow Preventers, 2021)
facts.fact: The antisiphon fill valve (ballcock) in a gravity water closet flush tank must meet ASSE 1002 or CSA B125.3. IPC 2021 Table 608.1 rates it for high hazard, backsiphonage only.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 608.1 (ICC PMG CodeNotes: Backflow Preventers, 2021)
facts.fact: A dual check valve backflow preventer (ASSE 1024) is a low hazard (pollution) device only, listed in IPC 2021 Table 608.1 in sizes 1/4 in to 1 in. It protects against back pressure and backsiphonage but is not testable like a double check assembly.
facts.note: ASSE 1024 is the standard for dual check valve devices; the CodeNote table lists the device's hazard and size range.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 608.1 (ICC PMG CodeNotes: Backflow Preventers, 2021)
facts.fact: A backflow preventer with an intermediate atmospheric vent (ASSE 1012 or CSA B64.3) is rated for low hazard only, against back pressure or backsiphonage. That is why IPC 2021 allows it on a boiler fill line only when no chemical conditioners are added.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 608.1 (ICC PMG CodeNotes: Backflow Preventers, 2021)
facts.fact: Hose connection vacuum breakers (ASSE 1011, sizes 1/2, 3/4 and 1 in) and frost-resistant, automatic-draining vacuum breaker wall hydrants (ASSE 1019, sizes 3/4 and 1 in) are rated in IPC 2021 Table 608.1 for high or low hazard, against backsiphonage or low head back pressure only.

facts.source: Term used in IPC 2021 Table 608.1 (ICC 2021 IPC/UPC Essentials, Session 54)
facts.fact: Low head back pressure, the rating used in IPC Table 608.1 for hose connection devices, means a back pressure of 4.33 psi or less, which equals a 10 ft column of water.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 608.1; ASSE 1001 (ICC PMG CodeNotes: Backflow Preventers, 2021)
facts.fact: Pipe-applied atmospheric vacuum breakers (ASSE 1001) are listed in sizes 1/2 in to 4 in for high or low hazard, backsiphonage only. Because an AVB may not stay under continuous pressure for 12 hours or more, no shutoff valve may be placed downstream of it.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 608.1 (ICC PMG CodeNotes: Backflow Preventers, 2021)
facts.fact: Fire sprinkler detector assemblies have their own standards in IPC 2021 Table 608.1: the double check detector fire protection assembly is ASSE 1048 (low hazard) and the reduced pressure detector fire protection assembly is ASSE 1047 (high or low hazard).

Testable backflow assemblies (RP, double check, PVB, spill-resistant VB, detector assemblies and hose connection backflow preventers) must be field tested using the ASSE 5000-series procedures (such as ASSE 5013, 5015, 5020, 5047, 5048, 5052, 5056) or CSA B64.10 / B64.10.1.

facts.source: IPC 2021 906.1 (ICC 2021 Plumbing Venting brochure; 2006 Virginia Plumbing Code 916.1, the same IPC rule under its older number)
facts.fact: A stack vent or vent stack may never be smaller than one-half the diameter of the drainage stack it serves, and never smaller than 1-1/4 in, even where Table 906.1 lengths look generous. For example, a 4 in stack needs at least a 2 in vent stack.
facts.note: In the 2015 and earlier IPC, vent pipe sizing was Section 916 (Table 916.1); since 2018 it is 906.1 and Table 906.1, while the trap-to-vent table is now 909.1.

facts.fact: Combination waste and vent pipe capacity (IPC 2021 Table 915.2.2), horizontal branch or stack / connecting to a building drain or subdrain: 2 in = 3 / 4 DFU; 2-1/2 in = 6 / 26; 3 in = 12 / 31; 4 in = 20 / 50; 5 in = 160 / 250; 6 in = 360 / 575.

In a combination waste and vent system, the vertical drop (riser) from a fixture to the combination waste and vent pipe may be no more than 8 ft, while the horizontal combination pipe has no length limit. The pipe still may not slope more than 1/2 in per ft.

For island fixture venting, the vent (or branch vent for several island fixtures) must rise at least 6 in above the highest island fixture served before it connects to the vent going outdoors. Vent piping below the flood level rim is installed like drainage pipe, sized per 906.2, and needs cleanouts for rodding.

facts.source: IPC 2021 914.4 (ICC 2021 Plumbing Venting brochure; ICC 2021 IPC/UPC Essentials)
facts.fact: The relief vent on a circuit-vented branch (required with four or more water closets) may also serve as the drain for fixtures in the same branch interval, but the discharge into that relief vent is limited to 4 DFU.

In a waste stack vent system, the stack vent must be the same size as the waste stack, and any offset in the stack vent must be at least 6 in above the flood level rim of the highest fixture. Offsets in the waste stack itself are not allowed between the lowest and highest fixture connections.
facts.note: The ICC brochure describes the vent offset limit as 6 in above the highest branch connection; check the exact wording of 913.3 in the code book.

facts.fact: In an IPC 2021 single stack vent system (Section 917), a 3 in stack may serve no more than two water closets, and a 3 in stack is not permitted taller than 75 ft. Larger stacks are sized by Table 917.2 using stack height and DFU.
facts.note: Single stack venting was added to the IPC in 2015 (as 917).

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 403.1, A-3 worship (ICC 2021 IPC/UPC Essentials, Session 54)
facts.fact: Worked example: a church (Group A-3 place of worship) with 500 occupants splits 250 male / 250 female. Water closets: men 1 per 150 = 250/150 = 1.67, round up to 2; women 1 per 75 = 250/75 = 3.33, round up to 4.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 403.1, A-1 theater (ICC 2021 IPC/UPC Essentials, Session 54)
facts.fact: Worked example: a movie theater (Group A-1) with 250 occupants splits 125 male / 125 female. Water closets: men 1 per 125 = 1; women 1 per 65 = 1.9, round up to 2.
Under IPC 2021 410.2, drinking fountains are not required where the occupant load is 15 or fewer. The UPC 2021 (415.2) sets that threshold at 30 occupants.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Chapter 2; UPC 2021 Chapter 2 (ICC 2021 IPC/UPC Essentials, Session 54)
facts.fact: The IPC defines hot water as water at 110 F or higher. The UPC defines hot water as water at 120 F or higher.
Water supplied to pedicure chairs, footbaths and head shampoo sinks must be limited to no more than 120 F by an ASSE 1070 (or CSA B125.3) water temperature limiting device.
facts.note: Numbered 424.10 in the 2018 IPC before Chapter 4 was reorganized.

facts.fact: Multiple (gang) showers fed by one tempered water pipe must be controlled by an automatic temperature control mixing valve (ASSE 1069 or CSA B125.3), or each shower must have its own ASSE 1016 valve. Either way the maximum setting is limited to 120 F.
facts.note: Numbered 424.4 in the 2018 IPC.

facts.fact: The UPC requires a shower drain, trap and fixture drain of at least 2 in. The IPC allows 1-1/2 in for a shower with a total flow of 5.7 gpm or less.

A water heater temperature and pressure relief valve may have a temperature setting of no more than 210 F, and a pressure setting no higher than the heater's rated working pressure or 150 psi, whichever is less.

facts.source: IPC 2021 504.6 item 14 (ICC Building Safety Journal, CodeNotes: Water Heater Safety in the I-Codes; ICC Session 54)
facts.fact: New in the 2021 IPC: where insert fittings are used on relief valve discharge piping (common with PEX), the discharge pipe must be one nominal size larger than the relief valve outlet, and the end of the tubing must be secured.

facts.source: IPC 2021 605.4; 504.6 item 13 (ICC Building Safety Journal, CodeNotes: Water Heater Safety in the I-Codes)
facts.fact: Water distribution pipe must conform to NSF 61, and hot water distribution pipe and tubing must have a pressure rating of at least 100 psi at 180 F. Relief valve discharge piping must also be a material rated for this service.
Under IPC 2021 704.1, horizontal drains that discharge to a grease interceptor must slope at least 1/4 in per ft, even when the pipe is 3 in or larger. This keeps grease-laden waste moving.
facts.note: From an ICC training presentation on the 2021 IPC. Check the local edition, since the general table allows 1/8 in per ft for 3 to 6 in pipe.

facts.fact: Exceptions to the 2 in solids rule for pumps that receive water closet waste: a grinder pump or grinder ejector needs a discharge opening of at least 1-1/4 in, and a macerating toilet assembly serving a single water closet needs a discharge of at least 3/4 in.
An oil separator must be at least 2 ft deep below the invert of its discharge drain, and its outlet must have a water seal of at least 18 in. The IPC and UPC agree on both numbers.

A private well or pump suction line must be kept away from sources of contamination. Examples from IPC 2021 Table 608.18.1: septic tank 25 ft, farm silo 25 ft, subsurface disposal (drain) field 50 ft, barnyard or pasture 100 ft.
Water used for plumbing tests must come from a potable source.

facts.source: PDI-WH 201 (Watts ES-15 water hammer arrestor spec sheet; Josam Absorbotron catalog)
facts.fact: Water hammer arrestors (ASSE 1010) are sized by PDI-WH 201 size symbols using the water supply fixture units on the branch: A = 1 to 11 FU, B = 12 to 32, C = 33 to 60, D = 61 to 113, E = 114 to 154, F = 155 to 330.
facts.note: Industry standard (PDI), not IPC text; IPC 604.9 requires arrestors where quick-closing valves are used.

facts.source: PDI-WH 201 placement rules (Watts ES-15 spec sheet); Josam Absorbotron catalog
facts.fact: PDI placement: on a branch up to 20 ft long, one arrestor sized for the whole branch goes at the end of the branch, between the last two fixtures. On a branch over 20 ft, a second arrestor is added so the two together cover the branch fixture units. Arrestors go as close as possible to the quick-closing valve.
facts.note: 20 ft rule confirmed in one manufacturer sheet (Watts); Josam confirms the close-as-possible placement. PDI-WH 201 itself not reviewed.

facts.source: Energy Policy Act of 1992 / 10 CFR 430.32 (Plumbing Manufacturers International, Summary of Current Plumbing Provisions; Alliance for Water Efficiency, Water Efficiency Standards, Codes and Guidelines, 2019)
facts.fact: The federal (EPAct 1992) maximums match IPC 2021 Table 604.4: showerheads 2.5 gpm at 80 psi, lavatory and kitchen faucets 2.2 gpm at 60 psi, water closets 1.6 gallons per flush, and urinals 1.0 gallon per flush. Federal law still allows blowout-type water closets up to 3.5 gpf.

facts.source: EPA WaterSense specifications (Plumbing Manufacturers International WaterSense summary; Alliance for Water Efficiency, 2019)
facts.fact: EPA WaterSense (voluntary) labels require: toilets 1.28 gpf or less, urinals 0.5 gpf or less, lavatory faucets 1.5 gpm or less at 60 psi (but not below 0.8 gpm), and showerheads 2.0 gpm or less. The model IPC requires only the higher Table 604.4 limits, but some states and green codes require WaterSense fixtures.

IPC 2021 Table 906.1, 2 in drainage stack: with 12 DFU, a 1-1/4 in vent may run 30 ft, a 1-1/2 in vent 75 ft, and a 2 in vent 200 ft of developed length. With 20 DFU, those lengths drop to 26 ft, 50 ft and 150 ft.

IPC 2021 Table 906.1, 3 in drainage stack, maximum vent developed length for 1-1/2 / 2 / 2-1/2 / 3 in vents: 10 DFU = 42 / 150 / 360 / 1,040 ft; 21 DFU = 32 / 110 / 270 / 810 ft; 53 DFU = 27 / 94 / 230 / 680 ft; 102 DFU = 25 / 86 / 210 / 620 ft.

IPC 2021 Table 906.1, 4 in drainage stack, maximum vent developed length for 2 / 2-1/2 / 3 / 4 in vents: 43 DFU = 35 / 85 / 250 / 980 ft; 140 DFU = 27 / 65 / 200 / 750 ft; 320 DFU = 23 / 55 / 170 / 640 ft; 540 DFU = 21 / 50 / 150 / 580 ft.

facts.source: IPC 2021 917.4 (ICC 2021 Plumbing Venting brochure; NY DOS Code Outreach Issue 2021-5, Plumbing Vents)
facts.fact: In a single stack vent system taller than two branch intervals, horizontal branches may not connect to the stack on the lower two floors. Those fixtures drain to a separate stack that joins the building drain at least 10 pipe diameters downstream. A horizontal branch serving fixtures other than water closets is limited to 12 ft of developed length.
facts.note: NY DOS bulletin covers the 2020 Plumbing Code of New York State, which uses the same IPC Section 917 rules.

facts.source: IPC 2021 913 (NY DOS Code Outreach Issue 2021-5, Plumbing Vents; ICC 2021 Plumbing Venting brochure)
facts.fact: A waste stack vent system may not receive water closet or urinal discharge. The waste stack must be vertical, one size from bottom to top (sized by Table 913.4), with no offsets between the highest and lowest fixture drain connections.

facts.source: IPC 2021 1002.4.1.5 (ICC Building Safety Journal, Significant Changes to Fixture Drains Serving as a Trap Priming Method in the 2021 IPC)
facts.fact: New in the 2021 IPC (1002.4.1.5): the entire waste flow from a lavatory or hand sink may be routed to a floor drain, trench drain or floor sink to keep that trap seal from drying out, as an alternative to a separate trap primer.

facts.source: NFPA 99 pipe labeling colors (Amico pipe marker label specification; Wikipedia, Pipe marking, citing NFPA 99C)
facts.fact: NFPA 99 medical gas pipe label colors (text on background): oxygen white on green; medical air black on yellow; nitrous oxide white on blue; nitrogen white on black; medical-surgical vacuum black on white; WAGD white on violet (purple); carbon dioxide black or white on gray; instrument air white on red.
facts.note: Check the edition of NFPA 99 adopted locally.

facts.source: NFPA 99 piping labeling (pipemarker.com NFPA 99 guide); IPC 2021 1202.1
facts.fact: Medical gas piping labels must appear at intervals of no more than 20 ft, at least once in or above every room, on both sides of walls or partitions the pipe passes through, and at least once in every story height a riser passes through.
facts.note: Source quotes NFPA 99C (2002); current NFPA 99 keeps similar labeling rules, but confirm the adopted edition.

facts.source: NFPA 99 installer testing (Plumbing & Mechanical magazine, Mandatory Testing of Medical Gas Systems)
facts.fact: After installation, positive-pressure medical gas piping gets a standing pressure test with oil-free dry nitrogen at 20% above normal line pressure for 24 hours. Final system verification is done by a verifier qualified to ASSE 6030, not by the installer.
facts.note: Article cites NFPA 99-2002; check the current adopted NFPA 99 edition for exact test values.

facts.source: PDI G-101 sizing method (Josam Interceptor Sizing guide; City of Independence, MO FOG sizing requirements)
facts.fact: Hydromechanical grease interceptor sizing by fixture volume (PDI G-101): sink volume in cubic inches (L x W x D) / 231 = gallons; take 75% of that (the rest is displaced by dishes); divide by a 1-minute drain period (2 minutes if allowed) to get gpm, and pick the next larger standard size.
facts.note: Industry method used with IPC 1003.3 hydromechanical interceptors rated by ASME A112.14.3 / PDI G101.

facts.source: Josam Interceptor Sizing guide (PDI G-101 method worked example)
facts.fact: Worked example: a 48 x 24 x 12 in sink holds 13,824 cu in / 231 = 59.8 gallons. At 75%, the load is 44.9 gallons. With a 1-minute drain period that is 44.9 gpm, so a 50 gpm interceptor is chosen; with a 2-minute period it is 22.5 gpm, so a 25 gpm unit.

facts.source: IPC 2021 1003.3.5, Table 1003.3.5.1 (ICC 2021 IPC/UPC Essentials); NYC 15 RCNY 19-11(e)
facts.fact: A hydromechanical grease interceptor's grease retention capacity in pounds must be at least twice its flow rating in gpm. For example, a 20 gpm interceptor must hold at least 40 lb of grease, and a 50 gpm unit at least 100 lb.
facts.note: The ICC session confirms the IPC table rates retention in pounds; the 2-to-1 ratio is confirmed in the NYC rule and matches the IPC table values.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 308.5 (Connecticut State Building Inspector code change proposal 22-004 quoting 2021 IPC/IRC hanger tables)
facts.fact: IPC 2021 Table 308.5: PE-RT and polypropylene (PP) pipe 1 in and smaller need horizontal support every 2.67 ft (32 in); 1-1/4 in and larger every 4 ft. Vertical support is every 10 ft, with a mid-story guide.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 308.5; IRC 2021 Table P2605.1 (Connecticut code change proposal 22-004)
facts.fact: CPVC pipe 1 in and smaller needs horizontal support every 3 ft, and CPVC 1-1/4 in and larger every 4 ft. Vertical support is every 10 ft with a mid-story guide.
facts.note: The proposal document shows these values in the IRC table; the IPC row shows 3 ft for both sizes, likely a transcription issue. Confirm against the code book.

facts.source: UPC Table 313.3 (as adopted in Minnesota Rules 4714.0313)
facts.fact: UPC hanger spacing for copper tube and pipe: 1-1/2 in and smaller every 6 ft horizontally, 2 in and larger every 10 ft; vertically at each floor, not over 10 ft. The IPC uses 6 ft only for 1-1/4 in and smaller copper tubing.
facts.note: Minnesota amends parts of UPC Table 313.3; these rows match the model UPC.

facts.source: UPC Table 313.3 (as adopted in Minnesota Rules 4714.0313)
facts.fact: UPC support for hubless cast iron: support every other joint, but at every joint where the pipe is over 4 ft long, with no hanger on the coupling itself. Vertically: at the base and each floor, not over 15 ft.

facts.source: UPC Table 313.3 (as adopted in Minnesota Rules 4714.0313)
facts.fact: UPC support for steel water or DWV pipe: 3/4 in and smaller every 10 ft, 1 in and larger every 12 ft horizontally; vertically every other floor, not over 25 ft. The IPC uses 12 ft horizontal and 15 ft vertical for all steel pipe.
Worked example: a building drain starts at invert elevation 100.00 ft and runs 120 ft at 1/8 in per ft. It falls 120 x 0.125 = 15 in = 1.25 ft, so the downstream invert is 98.75 ft.
facts.note: Derived calculation.

facts.fact: To find slope from a measured fall, divide the fall by the length. A 50 ft drain that drops 6-1/4 in has a slope of 6.25 / 50 = 0.125 in per ft, which is 1/8 in per ft (about 1%).
facts.note: Derived calculation.

facts.fact: A 10 ft head of water (the IPC DWV water test) puts 10 x 0.433 = 4.33 psi on the lowest joint. The 5 psi air test is roughly equal to 11.5 ft of water head (5 x 2.31).
facts.note: Derived calculation.

facts.fact: A 50-gallon water heater holds about 50 x 8.34 = 417 lb of water, plus the weight of the tank. This matters when a heater is placed in an attic or on a platform.
facts.note: Derived calculation.

facts.source: Plumbing math (heat): Btu = gallons x 8.34 x temperature rise
facts.fact: Heat needed to warm water: Btu = gallons x 8.34 x temperature rise (F). Example: heating 40 gallons from 50 F to 120 F takes 40 x 8.34 x 70 = 23,352 Btu.
facts.note: Derived calculation (1 Btu raises 1 lb of water 1 F).

facts.fact: Water heater recovery in gallons per hour = output Btu/h / (8.34 x temperature rise). Example: a 40,000 Btu/h burner at 80% efficiency delivers 32,000 Btu/h; with a 90 F rise, recovery = 32,000 / (8.34 x 90) = about 42.6 gph.
facts.note: Derived calculation.

facts.fact: Flow in gpm = 2.448 x (inside diameter in inches) squared x velocity in ft per second. Example: a 1 in pipe flowing at 8 fps carries about 2.448 x 1 x 8 = 19.6 gpm.
facts.note: Derived: 448.8 gpm per cfs x 0.005454 sq ft per square inch of diameter = 2.448.

facts.fact: Common plumbing temperatures in Celsius: 110 F = 43 C (tempered water limit), 120 F = 49 C (shower and tub limit), 140 F = 60 C (tankless and master mixing valve limit), 210 F = 99 C (T&P relief setting).
facts.note: Derived calculation, rounded to the nearest degree.

facts.source: Plumbing math (hydrostatics): 1 psi = 2.31 ft of head
facts.fact: To get a given static pressure from elevation alone, multiply psi by 2.31. A gravity tank must sit about 20 x 2.31 = 46.2 ft above a fixture to give it 20 psi, before friction loss.
facts.note: Derived calculation.

facts.fact: Worked example for continuous flow: a 1.5 gpm condensate pump discharging to a sanitary drain counts as 1.5 x 2 = 3 DFU, and a 6 gpm sump pump counts as 12 DFU.
facts.note: Derived from the 2 DFU per gpm rule.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Appendix E, Table E103.3(2) (Town of Eagle, CO plumbing calculation worksheet citing IPC Appendix E; City of Louisville, CO commercial water fixture count form)
facts.fact: IPC Appendix E water supply fixture units (WSFU) for a private bathroom group: with a flush tank water closet, 2.7 cold, 1.5 hot, 3.6 total; with a flush valve water closet, 6.0 cold, 3.0 hot, 8.0 total.
facts.note: Confirmed in two municipal sizing documents; the Eagle worksheet cites the 2015 IPC Appendix E, which carries into 2021. Appendix E applies only where adopted.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Appendix E, Table E103.3(2) (Town of Eagle, CO and City of Louisville, CO sizing documents)
facts.fact: Private fixture WSFU totals from IPC Table E103.3(2): lavatory 0.7; kitchen sink 1.4; bathtub 1.4; shower head 1.4; clothes washer (8 lb) 1.4; dishwasher 1.4 (hot only); bidet 2.0; water closet with flush tank 2.2; water closet with flush valve 6.0.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Appendix E, Table E103.3(2) (City of Louisville, CO commercial water fixture count form)
facts.fact: Public fixture WSFU totals from IPC Table E103.3(2): water closet with flush valve 10; water closet with flush tank 5; urinal with 1 in flush valve 10, 3/4 in flush valve 5, flush tank 3; lavatory 2.0; shower head 4.0; hotel or restaurant kitchen sink 4.0; service sink 3.0.
facts.note: Values match the Town of Eagle worksheet where both list the fixture.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Appendix E, Table E103.3(2) (City of Louisville, CO commercial water fixture count form)
facts.fact: Other WSFU values in IPC Table E103.3(2): hose bibb 2.5; drinking fountain 0.25; water closet with flushometer tank (public or private) 2.0; laundry tray 1.4 (private); public bathtub 4.0.

In Table E103.3(2), a fixture's total WSFU is less than its cold plus hot values (a private lavatory is 0.5 cold + 0.5 hot but 0.7 total) because both are not drawn at full rate at once. Use the total column for the water service and any main that feeds both hot and cold (ahead of the water heater), the cold column for cold-only branches, and the hot column for hot water piping.
facts.note: Values confirmed in municipal sizing documents; the use of each column follows the Appendix E method.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Appendix E, Table E103.3(2); plumbing math
facts.fact: Worked example: a house with two private bathroom groups (flush tank, 3.6 each), a kitchen sink (1.4), a dishwasher (1.4), a clothes washer (1.4) and two hose bibbs (2.5 each) totals 7.2 + 1.4 + 1.4 + 1.4 + 5.0 = 16.4 WSFU. That total is then converted to gpm demand with Table E103.3(3).
facts.note: Derived from the table values above.

facts.source: AWWA C651 (Plastics Pipe Institute TR-34; American Water specification 33 01 10.15); allowed by IPC 2021 610.1
facts.fact: AWWA C651 continuous feed method (an allowed alternative to the IPC 610.1 procedure): chlorinate the new main to about 25 mg/L free chlorine, and after 24 hours the residual must still be at least 10 mg/L. The tablet method uses about 25 mg/L held at least 24 hours (48 hours if the water is below 41 F).

facts.source: AWWA C651 slug method (Plastics Pipe Institute TR-34; American Water specification 33 01 10.15)
facts.fact: AWWA C651 slug method: a slug of water at about 100 mg/L free chlorine is moved through the main so every part is exposed for at least 3 hours. If the residual drops below 50 mg/L, flow is stopped and chlorine is added to bring it back to at least 100 mg/L.

facts.source: IPC 2021 609.2.1 (ICC Building Safety Journal, Significant Changes to Tracer Wire for Buried Nonmetallic Water Service Piping; ICC 2021 IPC/UPC Essentials)
facts.fact: New in the 2021 IPC (609.2.1): buried nonmetallic water service piping serving a hospital (Group I-2, Condition 2) needs a tracer wire at least 18 AWG with insulation listed for direct burial, accessible at each end of the piping.
facts.note: 2024 IPC adds a 14 AWG tracer wire for plastic sewer piping (306.2.4).

facts.source: IPC 2021 708.1.5 Exception 1, 708.1.6 (ICC Building Safety Journal, Significant Changes to Removable Fixture Traps Serving as Cleanouts)
facts.fact: Under the 2021 IPC, a removable P-trap may serve as cleanout access only for drain pipe the same size as the trap or one size larger. New Section 708.1.6 also accepts removable fixtures with integral traps (such as water closets and urinals) as cleanout access, but removing a water closet does not count as the cleanout for a building sewer.

facts.source: IPC 2021 403.1.2 (ICC Building Safety Journal, Significant Changes to Fixtures in Single-User Toilet Rooms)
facts.fact: Under IPC 2021 403.1.2, fixtures in single-user toilet rooms and bathing rooms count toward the building's total required fixtures. Required fixtures may be in single-user rooms, in rooms separated by sex, or a mix of both.

facts.source: IPC 2021 403.2 Exception 6; 405.3.4 (ICC Building Safety Journal, Significant Changes to Multiple-User Nonseparated Toilet Facilities)
facts.fact: The 2021 IPC (403.2, Exception 6) allows multiple-user toilet rooms designed to serve both sexes. Each water closet must be in a private compartment per 405.3.4, and any urinals in such a room must be in stalls.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 709.1 (existing text shown in ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, proposal P1-21)
facts.fact: More IPC 2021 Table 709.1 values: dental unit or cuspidor 1 DFU; dental lavatory 1 DFU; combination sink and tray 2 DFU; wash sink (circular or multiple) 2 DFU for each set of faucets; plain sink 2 DFU; kitchen sink with a disposer, dishwasher or both is still 2 DFU.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 709.1 footnote b (ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, P1-21)
facts.fact: Per IPC 2021 Table 709.1 footnote b, a showerhead installed over a bathtub or whirlpool tub does not increase the tub's DFU value, so a tub/shower combination stays at 2 DFU.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 709.1 footnotes a, d, e (ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, P1-21)
facts.fact: Table 709.1 footnotes: water closet and urinal trap sizes must match the fixture outlet size; fixtures with traps larger than 3 in are rated using Table 709.2; and for building drain and sewer loads, water closets and urinals may not be given a lower DFU value unless testing confirms it.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 709.1 footnotes f, g, h (ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, P1-21)
facts.fact: When a fixture is added to a bathroom group, its DFU value is added to the group's 5 or 6 DFU. Floor sinks have no fixed DFU in Table 709.1; they are rated per 709.4 and 709.4.1 by what drains into them. Clothes washer standpipe drain, branch and stack sizing is covered in 406.2.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 403.1, A-4 and A-5 (existing text shown in ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, P22-21)
facts.fact: IPC 2021 Table 403.1 for arenas and stadiums (A-4 and A-5): water closets for men 1 per 75 for the first 1,500 and 1 per 120 after that; for women 1 per 40 for the first 1,520 and 1 per 60 after that. Lavatories: men 1 per 200, women 1 per 150. Drinking fountains 1 per 1,000.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 403.1, A-3 (ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, P22-21)
facts.fact: IPC 2021 Table 403.1 for auditoriums without permanent seating, museums, libraries, galleries and gyms (A-3): water closets men 1 per 125, women 1 per 65; lavatories 1 per 200; drinking fountains 1 per 500; one service sink. Places of worship use 1 per 150 (men) and 1 per 75 (women) with drinking fountains 1 per 1,000.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 403.1, F and S (ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, P22-21)
facts.fact: IPC 2021 Table 403.1: factories and industrial buildings (F-1, F-2) need water closets 1 per 100, lavatories 1 per 100, drinking fountains 1 per 400 and one service sink. Storage buildings and warehouses (S-1, S-2) need water closets 1 per 100, lavatories 1 per 100, drinking fountains 1 per 1,000 and one service sink.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 403.1, R-2 and R-1 (ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, P22-21)
facts.fact: IPC 2021 Table 403.1: apartment houses (R-2) need 1 water closet, 1 lavatory, 1 bathtub or shower and 1 kitchen sink per dwelling unit, plus 1 automatic clothes washer connection per 20 dwelling units. Hotels and motels (R-1) need 1 water closet, 1 lavatory and 1 bathtub or shower per sleeping unit, plus a service sink.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 403.1, dormitories (ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, P22-21)
facts.fact: IPC 2021 Table 403.1 for dormitories, fraternities, sororities and boarding houses (not transient): water closets 1 per 10, lavatories 1 per 10, bathtubs or showers 1 per 8, drinking fountains 1 per 100 and one service sink. Congregate living facilities with 16 or fewer persons use the same ratios.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 403.1, I-2 (ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, P22-21)
facts.fact: IPC 2021 Table 403.1 for hospitals and nursing homes (I-2): patients need 1 water closet and 1 lavatory per room; employees need water closets 1 per 25 and lavatories 1 per 35; visitors need water closets 1 per 75 and lavatories 1 per 100. One service sink is required per floor.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 403.1, A-2 casinos (ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, P22-21)
facts.fact: IPC 2021 Table 403.1 for casino gaming areas (A-2): water closets for men 1 per 100 for the first 400 and 1 per 250 after that; for women 1 per 50 for the first 400 and 1 per 150 after that. Drinking fountains 1 per 1,000.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 403.1, I-3 and I-4 (ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, P22-21)
facts.fact: IPC 2021 Table 403.1: prisons need 1 water closet and 1 lavatory per cell; reformatories, detention and correctional centers need water closets and lavatories 1 per 15; adult and child day care facilities need water closets and lavatories 1 per 15, with drinking fountains 1 per 100.
Worked example: an outdoor stadium (A-5) with 4,000 occupants has 2,000 women. Water closets for women = 1,520/40 + 480/60 = 38 + 8 = 46.
facts.note: Derived from the A-5 ratios.

facts.source: IPC 2021 403.1.1 (existing text shown in ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, P25-21/P26-21)
facts.fact: Under IPC 2021 403.1.1, when a building has more than one occupancy, the fractional fixture counts for each occupancy are added together first, and only then rounded up to the next whole fixture.

facts.source: IPC 2021 403.1.1 Exceptions 2 and 3 (ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, P25-21/P26-21)
facts.fact: IPC 2021 403.1.1 Exception 2: for multiple-user toilet facilities serving all genders, the fixture count is figured on 100% of the total occupant load (not split 50/50), and any urinal must be in a stall. Exception 3: no split by sex is needed where single-user water closets and bathing fixtures are provided per 403.1.2.

facts.source: IPC 2021 405.3.4 Exceptions (ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, P39-21)
facts.fact: Exceptions to the IPC 2021 405.3.4 water closet compartment rule: a single-occupant toilet room with a lockable door; a child day care toilet room with two or more water closets may have one without a compartment; and toilet areas in Group I-3 (jail) housing areas.

facts.source: IPC 2021 405.3.5 Exceptions (ICC 2021 Group A Public Comment Agenda, P39-21)
facts.fact: Urinal privacy partitions (IPC 2021 405.3.5) are not required in a single-occupant or family/assisted-use toilet room with a lockable door. A child day care toilet room with two or more urinals may have one urinal without partitions.
Where drinking fountains are required, the IPC requires at least two: one at wheelchair height and one for standing persons.
facts.note: Check the 410.3 exceptions, such as a single unit that serves both heights.

facts.fact: The UPC lets urinals be closer together than the IPC: at least 12 in from the urinal centerline to a side wall or partition and 24 in center to center. The IPC uses 15 in to a side wall and 30 in center to center for urinals.

A reduced pressure principle backflow preventer may be under continuous pressure, but it must be accessible for testing and may not be installed below grade (such as in a pit) where it could be submerged. Its relief port must discharge through an air gap.

The Table 909.1 trap arm limits for small pipes equal the distance at which the fall reaches one pipe diameter: 1-1/4 in x 5 ft, 1-1/2 in x 6 ft and 2 in x 8 ft at 1/4 in per ft each fall exactly their own diameter. This matches 909.2, which says the total fall may not exceed the fixture drain diameter.
facts.note: Derived from Table 909.1 values (1-1/4: 5 ft, 1-1/2: 6 ft, 2: 8 ft at 1/4 in per ft).

facts.fact: Worked example: a 10 in offset made with 22-1/2 degree fittings needs a travel of 10 x 2.613 = 26.1 in and a run (setback) of 10 x 2.414 = 24.1 in, center to center.
facts.note: Derived calculation.

facts.fact: Worked example: a 12 in offset made with 60 degree fittings needs a travel of 12 x 1.155 = 13.9 in and a run of 12 x 0.577 = 6.9 in.
facts.note: Derived calculation.

facts.fact: Worked example: 200 ft of 2 in pipe holds 200 x 0.163 = 32.6 gal. Household bleach at 5.25% is 52,500 ppm, so a 50 ppm dose needs 32.6 x 50 / 52,500 = 0.031 gal of bleach, about 4 fluid ounces.
facts.note: Derived calculation.

facts.fact: Building drain sizing examples from Table 710.1(1): 200 DFU at 1/4 in per ft fits a 4 in drain (216 max), but at 1/8 in per ft it needs a 5 in drain (4 in is only 180). 40 DFU at 1/8 in per ft needs a 4 in drain (3 in is only 36).
facts.note: Derived from Table 710.1(1) values.

facts.fact: Horizontal branch sizing examples from Table 710.1(2): four lavatories (4 DFU) fit a 2 in branch (6 max); 10 DFU of sinks needs 2-1/2 in (12 max); 18 DFU needs 3 in (20 max). Any branch serving a water closet must still be at least 3 in.
facts.note: Derived from Table 710.1(2) values.

facts.fact: Stack sizing example: a 3 in stack with four branch intervals may carry up to 72 DFU total, but no single branch interval may put more than 20 DFU into it. A 3 in stack with only three branch intervals is limited to 48 DFU.
facts.note: Derived from Table 710.1(2) values.

facts.fact: Static pressure limits how high water can go: a 60 psi main can lift water at most 60 x 2.31 = 138.6 ft with no flow. To have 15 psi at a fixture 80 ft above the meter, you need at least 80 x 0.433 + 15 = 49.6 psi at the meter, plus friction loss.
facts.note: Derived calculation.

facts.fact: Worked example: a 4 in vertical leader rated 192 gpm can serve 192 / (4 x 0.0104) = about 4,615 sq ft of roof at a 4 in/hr design rainfall.
facts.note: Derived from the Table 1106.3 rating and the 1106.2.1 formula.

facts.fact: IPC 2021 Table 917.2 (single stack vent), maximum DFU by stack size for stacks under 75 ft / 75 to under 160 ft / 160 ft and over: 3 in = 24 / not permitted / not permitted; 4 in = 225 / 24 / NP; 5 in = 480 / 225 / 24; 6 in = 1,015 / 480 / 225; 8 in = 2,320 / 1,015 / 480.

Single stack vent details (IPC 2021 917): vertical fixture drain sections must be at least 2 in (3 in for standpipes and water-supplied urinals) and no more than 4 ft tall. A water closet on a 3 in branch may be no more than 4 ft (developed length) from the stack with a wye connection, or 8 ft with a sanitary tee. The stack vent is the same size as the stack.

Vent sizing examples under IPC 2021 906.2 (one-half the drain size, never less than 1-1/4 in): a 4 in drain needs at least a 2 in vent, a 3 in drain at least a 1-1/2 in vent, and 2 in or smaller drains at least a 1-1/4 in vent. If the vent runs more than 40 ft, go up one pipe size for the whole length.

Because a horizontal wet vent is limited to fixtures within two bathroom groups, ICC explains it can serve from 2 up to 10 fixtures, with no more than two fixtures of any one type. The wet vent pipe is sized larger than Chapter 7 would normally require so its upper part stays open for air.

Engineered vent systems (IPC 2021 Section 919) must be designed by a registered design professional and submitted for approval. Using the airflow method of 919.2 and Table 919.2, individual vents may be as small as 1/2 in.

Every hose-threaded outlet must be protected by an atmospheric vacuum breaker, a pressure vacuum breaker, or a permanently attached hose connection vacuum breaker. Exceptions: water heater and boiler drain valves, and hose bibbs that serve clothes washing machines.

facts.source: IPC 2021 608.14 vacuum breakers; IRC 2021 P2902 (ICC PMG CodeNotes: Backflow Preventers, 2021)
facts.fact: The IPC sets the critical level of vacuum breakers, including pressure vacuum breakers, at least 6 in above the flood level rim. The IRC requires PVBs and spill-resistant VBs to be at least 12 in above the highest downstream piping and the flood level rim.
facts.note: The UPC also uses 12 in for PVBs. Use the code your exam is based on.

facts.fact: Nonpotable outlets (hose connections, open-ended pipes, faucets) must carry a sign reading 'Nonpotable water is utilized for [application]. CAUTION: NONPOTABLE WATER - DO NOT DRINK.' along with the 'Do Not Drink' pictograph. Reclaimed, rain and gray water piping is identified in purple (608.8.2.1).
The IPC's annual inspection covers more than testable assemblies: air gaps must also be inspected each year to confirm the required clearances are still in place.

Worked example: a public restroom branch with three 1.6 gpf public water closets (4 DFU each), two urinals flushing 1 gallon or less (2 each) and three lavatories (1 each) carries 12 + 4 + 3 = 19 DFU. A 3 in horizontal branch (20 DFU max) is adequate.
facts.note: Derived from Table 709.1 and Table 710.1(2) values.

facts.fact: Vent stack example (Table 906.1): a 4 in stack carrying 320 DFU needs a vent 100 ft long. A 2-1/2 in vent is good for only 55 ft, but a 3 in vent is good for 170 ft, so use 3 in.
facts.note: Derived from Table 906.1 values.

facts.fact: Vent stack example (Table 906.1): a 3 in stack with 53 DFU and a 120 ft vent. A 2 in vent allows only 94 ft, so a 2-1/2 in vent (230 ft) is required.
facts.note: Derived from Table 906.1 values.

facts.fact: Wet vent example: a lavatory (1 DFU) and a bathtub (2 DFU) wet-vented through one pipe put 3 DFU on the wet vent. Table 912.3 allows 4 DFU on a 2 in wet vent, so 2 in works; 1-1/2 in would allow only 1 DFU.
facts.note: Derived from Table 912.3 values.

facts.fact: Combination waste and vent example: three floor drains (2 DFU each, 6 DFU total) on a horizontal combination waste and vent branch need at least 2-1/2 in pipe, since Table 915.2.2 allows only 3 DFU on 2 in and 6 DFU on 2-1/2 in.
facts.note: Derived from Table 915.2.2 values.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Appendix E, Table E103.3(2); plumbing math
facts.fact: WSFU example for a public restroom: four flush valve water closets (10 each) + two urinals with 3/4 in flush valves (5 each) + four public lavatories (2 each) = 40 + 10 + 8 = 58 WSFU.
facts.note: Derived from Table E103.3(2) values.

facts.fact: Fixture count example, restaurant (A-2) with 300 occupants: 150 per sex. Water closets 150/75 = 2 per sex; lavatories 150/200 = 0.75, round up to 1 per sex; drinking fountains by ratio 300/500 = 0.6, round up to 1 (provided at both wheelchair and standing heights per 410.3), or none if the restaurant serves free water in containers (410.4); 1 service sink.
facts.note: Derived from Table 403.1 ratios.

facts.fact: Fixture count example, retail store (M) with 1,600 occupants: 800 per sex. Water closets 800/500 = 1.6, round up to 2 per sex; lavatories 800/750 = 1.07, round up to 2 per sex; drinking fountains 1,600/1,000 = 1.6, round up to 2.
facts.note: Derived from Table 403.1 ratios.

facts.fact: Fixture count example, school (E) with 500 occupants: 250 per sex. Water closets 250/50 = 5 per sex; lavatories 250/50 = 5 per sex; drinking fountains 500/100 = 5; 1 service sink.
facts.note: Derived from Table 403.1 ratios.

facts.fact: Leader sizing example: a 15,000 sq ft roof at 2 in/hr produces 15,000 x 2 x 0.0104 = 312 gpm. A 4 in leader (192 gpm) is too small; a 5 in leader (360 gpm) works.
facts.note: Derived from Table 1106.3 values and the 1106.2.1 formula.

facts.fact: Oil separator example: a repair garage draining 2,500 sq ft needs 6 cu ft for the first 100 sq ft plus 24 cu ft for the remaining 2,400 sq ft (1 cu ft per 100 sq ft) = 30 cu ft.
facts.note: Derived from the 1003.4.2.2 sizing rule.

facts.fact: Worked example: 50 ft of 3 in pipe holds 50 x 0.367 = 18.4 gal of water, which weighs about 18.4 x 8.34 = 153 lb. Supports must carry the pipe plus this water weight.
facts.note: Derived calculation.

facts.fact: During a water test of a 30 ft tall stack filled to the top, the base fittings see 30 x 0.433 = 13 psi. That is why each test section is limited, and why the code asks only for a 10 ft head (4.33 psi) on each joint.
facts.note: Derived calculation.

facts.fact: A 1% slope equals 0.12 in per ft (1% of 12 in), which is just under 1/8 in per ft (0.125). A 2% slope is 0.24 in per ft, just under 1/4 in per ft.
facts.note: Derived calculation.

facts.source: IPC 2021 608.15.1 air gap rule; plumbing math
facts.fact: Air gap example for an opening larger than 1 in: a 1-1/4 in effective opening needs an air gap of 2 x 1.25 = 2.5 in away from walls, or 3 x 1.25 = 3.75 in where walls are close to the outlet.
facts.note: Derived from the air gap table rule for openings over 1 in.

facts.fact: Indirect waste air gap example: a 1 in indirect waste pipe must end at least 2 in (twice its effective opening) above the flood level rim of the receptor; a 1-1/2 in pipe needs at least 3 in.
facts.note: Derived from the 802.2.1 twice-the-opening rule.

facts.fact: The Table 909.1 trap-to-vent distance limits do not apply to self-siphoning fixtures such as water closets. The developed length from a water closet's trap weir to its vent is not limited by that table.
facts.note: Could not reach the IPC 2021 code text during research (ICC Digital Codes and UpCodes pages were not readable); stated from the published 909.1 exception. Confirm in the code book.

facts.fact: The pressure-reducing valve required when static pressure exceeds 80 psi must conform to ASSE 1003 or CSA B356 and must include a strainer.
facts.note: Code text not reachable during research; standard numbers stated from the published 604.8. Confirm in the code book.

facts.fact: Unfired hot water storage tanks must be insulated to at least R-12.5.
facts.note: Code text not reachable during research; confirm in the code book.

facts.fact: A drain valve must be installed at the bottom of every tank-type water heater and hot water storage tank. Its inlet must be at least 3/4 in nominal iron pipe size, and its outlet must have hose threads.
facts.note: Code text not reachable during research; confirm in the code book.

facts.fact: Roof drain strainers must extend at least 4 in above the roof surface around the drain. On roof decks, sun decks and similar areas, flat-surface strainers are allowed if their inlet area is at least twice the area of the leader or conductor they serve.
facts.note: Code text not reachable during research; subsection numbers not confirmed. Confirm in the code book.

facts.fact: Storm leaders and conductors may not be used as soil, waste or vent pipes, and soil, waste or vent pipes may not be used as storm conductors.
facts.note: Code text not reachable during research; subsection number not confirmed.

facts.fact: Plastic pipe, fittings and plastic pipe-related components must be third-party certified as conforming to NSF 14. Pipe and fittings that carry potable water must also meet NSF 61.
facts.note: Code text not reachable during research; subsection number not confirmed.

facts.fact: Required plumbing inspections include an underground inspection (after trenches are dug and bedded and pipe is installed, before backfill), a rough-in inspection (after the roof, framing, firestopping and bracing are in place, before covering), and a final inspection after the work is complete.
facts.note: Code text not reachable during research; confirm wording in the code book.

facts.fact: Hub-and-spigot cast-iron soil pipe joints use compression gaskets meeting ASTM C564. Hubless cast-iron joints use shielded couplings meeting CISPI 310, ASTM C1277 or ASTM C1540.
facts.note: Code text not reachable during research; subsection numbers not confirmed.

facts.fact: Soldered copper water joints must use flux meeting ASTM B813 and lead-free solder meeting ASTM B32, and must be made following ASTM B828.
facts.note: Code text not reachable during research; subsection numbers not confirmed.

facts.fact: Each plastic has its own solvent cement standard: PVC cement meets ASTM D2564 (with ASTM F656 primer), CPVC cement meets ASTM F493, and ABS cement meets ASTM D2235. Solvent-cement joints between different types of plastic are prohibited.
facts.note: Code text not reachable during research; PVC standards and the mixed-plastic prohibition are already in the existing knowledge base.

facts.fact: Joints between copper or copper-alloy tubing and galvanized steel pipe must be made with a copper-alloy (brass) fitting or a dielectric fitting or union meeting ASSE 1079, to limit galvanic corrosion.
facts.note: Code text not reachable during research; subsection number not confirmed.

facts.fact: Where drainage piping is roughed in for future fixtures, a vent rough-in must also be installed. It must be at least one-half the diameter of the rough-in drain it will serve and be marked to show it is a vent.
facts.note: Code text not reachable during research; section number recalled from the 2018/2021 IPC. Confirm in the code book.

facts.fact: Cleanout spacing example: a straight 230 ft horizontal building drain needs cleanouts no more than 100 ft apart, so at least two intermediate cleanouts are needed in addition to the one near the building drain and sewer junction.
facts.note: Derived from the 100 ft cleanout spacing rule.

facts.fact: Hot water distance example: a lavatory 65 ft (developed length) from the water heater exceeds the 50 ft limit, so a recirculating loop or heat-traced pipe must bring the hot water source to within 50 ft of the fixture.
facts.note: Derived from the 607.2 rule.

facts.fact: Fixture count example: an indoor arena (A-4) with 3,000 occupants has 1,500 men. Water closets for men = 1,500/75 = 20 (the 1 per 120 rate applies only above 1,500).
facts.note: Derived from Table 403.1 ratios.

facts.fact: Branch interval example: a drainage stack with a horizontal branch on each of six floors, about 10 ft apart, has six branch intervals. Because that is five or more, the stack needs a vent stack.
facts.note: Derived from the 904.2 rule and branch interval definition.

facts.source: IPC 2021 Table 403.1, Group B; plumbing math
facts.fact: Fixture count example, office (B) with 300 occupants: 150 per sex. Water closets per sex = 50/25 + 100/50 = 2 + 2 = 4. Lavatories per sex = 80/40 + 70/80 = 2 + 0.875 = 2.875, round up to 3. Drinking fountains = 300/100 = 3.
facts.note: Derived from Table 403.1 ratios (B: water closets 1 per 25 for first 50, then 1 per 50; lavatories 1 per 40 for first 80, then 1 per 80).

facts.fact: Urinal substitution example: if an office needs 4 water closets for men, urinals may replace up to 50% of them (2). In an assembly or educational occupancy needing 6 water closets for men, urinals may replace up to 67%, which is 4.
facts.note: Derived from the 424.2 substitution limits (67% assembly/educational, 50% others).

facts.fact: Wall runoff example: a 2,000 sq ft roof has a 20 ft high by 50 ft long wall that drains onto it. Half the wall area (1,000 / 2 = 500 sq ft) is added, so drains and leaders are sized for 2,500 sq ft.
facts.note: Derived from the 1106.4 one-half wall area rule.

facts.fact: Residential DFU example: three bathroom groups with 1.6 gpf water closets (5 each = 15), a kitchen sink (2), a dishwasher (2) and a clothes washer (2) total 21 DFU. A 3 in building drain at 1/8 in per ft is limited to 36 DFU, so 3 in works even at the flatter slope.
facts.note: Derived from Table 709.1 and Table 710.1(1) values.

questions.q: Under IPC 2021 Table 608.1, a spill-resistant vacuum breaker (ASSE 1056) protects against:
questions.why: Like a pressure vacuum breaker, the SVB is rated for high or low hazard but backsiphonage only.

questions.q: The antisiphon fill valve in a gravity toilet tank must comply with which standard?
questions.why: Antisiphon fill valves for gravity flush tanks are ASSE 1002 (or CSA B125.3) devices.

questions.q: Low head back pressure is back pressure of no more than:
questions.why: Low head back pressure is 4.33 psi or less, equal to a 10 ft column of water.

questions.q: The maximum temperature setting allowed for a water heater temperature relief valve is:
questions.why: T&P valves may be set no higher than 210 F, and no higher than 150 psi or the heater's rating.

questions.q: Relief valve discharge piping made with insert fittings (such as PEX) must be:
c: The same size as the valve outlet
One nominal size larger than the valve outlet
At least 1 in regardless of outlet size
Two nominal sizes larger than the valve outlet
questions.why: Insert fittings reduce the bore, so the 2021 IPC requires the pipe to be one nominal size larger than the outlet.

questions.q: Per IPC 2021 Table 915.2.2, a 3 in combination waste and vent pipe serving as a horizontal branch may carry up to:
questions.why: A 3 in horizontal combination waste and vent carries 12 DFU; 31 DFU applies when it connects to a building drain.

questions.q: A church (A-3 worship) has 500 occupants. How many water closets are required for women (1 per 75)?
questions.why: Half the load is 250 women; 250/75 = 3.33, which rounds up to 4.

questions.q: Under the UPC, the minimum size of a shower drain and trap is:
questions.why: The UPC requires a 2 in shower drain and trap; the IPC allows 1-1/2 in for most showers.

questions.q: The outlet of an oil separator must have a water seal of at least:
questions.why: Oil separators need at least an 18 in water seal and must be at least 2 ft deep below the discharge invert.

questions.q: A PDI size C water hammer arrestor is rated for a branch load of:
Gang showers supplied by one tempered water pipe may be controlled by an automatic temperature control mixing valve meeting:
questions.why: ASSE 1069 covers automatic temperature control mixing valves for gang showers, limited to 120 F.

questions.q: A grinder pump that receives water closet waste must have a discharge opening of at least:
questions.why: Grinder pumps are an exception to the 2 in solids rule and need at least a 1-1/4 in discharge.

questions.q: What is the WaterSense maximum flush volume for a toilet?
questions.why: WaterSense toilets use 1.28 gpf or less; the IPC and federal limit is 1.6 gpf.

questions.q: Federal law still allows which type of water closet to use up to 3.5 gallons per flush?
questions.why: Blowout water closets are the federal exception at 3.5 gpf; others are limited to 1.6 gpf.

questions.q: Per IPC 2021 Table 906.1, a 3 in stack with 102 DFU may use a 2 in vent stack up to what developed length?
questions.why: For a 3 in stack at 102 DFU: 1-1/2 in = 25 ft, 2 in = 86 ft, 2-1/2 in = 210 ft, 3 in = 620 ft.

questions.q: Per IPC 2021 Table 906.1, a 4 in stack carrying 540 DFU with a 3 in vent stack may have a vent developed length up to:
questions.why: At 540 DFU on a 4 in stack, a 3 in vent may run 150 ft; a 4 in vent may run 580 ft.

questions.q: Which fixtures may NOT discharge into a waste stack vent system?
questions.why: A waste stack vent carries waste only; water closets and urinals are not allowed to connect.

questions.q: Under NFPA 99, an oxygen pipe label has:
questions.why: Oxygen is white on green; medical air is black on yellow and nitrous oxide is white on blue.

questions.q: When sizing a hydromechanical grease interceptor by sink volume (PDI method), what percentage of the sink volume is used as the drainage load?
questions.why: Sinks are assumed 75% full because dishes displace about 25% of the water.

questions.q: A 25 gpm hydromechanical grease interceptor must have a grease retention capacity of at least:
questions.why: Grease retention capacity in pounds must be at least twice the flow rating in gpm: 25 x 2 = 50 lb.

questions.q: Under IPC 2021 Table 308.5, 3/4 in PE-RT tubing must be supported horizontally at least every:
questions.why: PE-RT (like PEX and PP) 1 in and smaller needs support every 2.67 ft, which is 32 in.

questions.q: Under the UPC, horizontal support spacing for 1-1/2 in copper tube is:
questions.why: The UPC uses 6 ft for copper 1-1/2 in and smaller and 10 ft for 2 in and larger.

questions.q: A drain runs 120 ft at 1/8 in per ft from an invert of 100.00 ft. What is the downstream invert?
How many Btu does it take to heat 40 gallons of water from 50 F to 120 F?
questions.ref: Btu = gal x 8.34 x temp rise

questions.q: About how many gpm flow through a 1 in pipe at 8 ft per second?
questions.why: 2.448 x 1 squared x 8 = 19.6 gpm.

questions.q: A 6 gpm sump pump discharging continuously into a sanitary drain counts as how many DFU?
questions.why: Continuous flow is counted at 2 DFU per gpm, so 6 x 2 = 12 DFU.

questions.q: Under IPC Appendix E, the total water supply fixture unit value for a private bathroom group with a flush tank water closet is:
questions.why: A private bathroom group with a flush tank is 3.6 WSFU total (8.0 with a flush valve).

questions.q: Per IPC Table E103.3(2), a public water closet with a flush valve is rated at how many WSFU?
questions.why: Public flush valve water closets are 10 WSFU; public flush tank closets are 5.

questions.q: Per IPC Table E103.3(2), a hose bibb is rated at:
questions.why: A hose bibb counts as 2.5 water supply fixture units.

questions.q: Using the AWWA C651 continuous feed method, after 24 hours the free chlorine residual must be at least:
questions.why: The main is dosed to about 25 mg/L, and at least 10 mg/L must remain after 24 hours.

questions.q: Under IPC 2021 609.2.1, tracer wire for a hospital's buried nonmetallic water service must be at least:
questions.why: The 2021 IPC requires at least 18 AWG tracer wire listed for direct burial.

questions.q: Under the 2021 IPC, a removable P-trap may serve as cleanout access for drain pipe that is:
c: The same size or one size larger than the trap
Two sizes larger than the trap
questions.why: A removable P-trap counts as cleanout access only for pipe of the same size or one size larger.

questions.q: Per IPC 2021 Table 709.1, a dental unit or cuspidor is rated at:
questions.why: Dental units, cuspidors and dental lavatories are each 1 DFU.

questions.q: A bathtub with a showerhead over it has what DFU value under IPC 2021 Table 709.1?
questions.why: A showerhead over a tub does not raise the tub's 2 DFU value.

questions.q: For an apartment building (R-2), IPC 2021 Table 403.1 requires automatic clothes washer connections at a rate of:
questions.why: R-2 apartment houses need 1 automatic clothes washer connection per 20 dwelling units.

questions.q: In a factory (F-1), IPC 2021 Table 403.1 requires drinking fountains at:
questions.why: Factories need 1 drinking fountain per 400 occupants, with water closets and lavatories at 1 per 100.

questions.q: In a dormitory, IPC 2021 Table 403.1 requires bathtubs or showers at a rate of:
questions.why: Dormitories need 1 bathtub or shower per 8 occupants, and water closets and lavatories at 1 per 10.

questions.q: An outdoor stadium has 2,000 women. Using IPC Table 403.1 (1 per 40 for the first 1,520, then 1 per 60), how many water closets are needed for women?
questions.why: 1,520/40 = 38 plus 480/60 = 8, for 46 water closets.

questions.q: Under IPC 2021 403.1.1, a multiple-user toilet room serving all genders has its fixture count based on:
questions.why: All-gender multiple-user facilities are figured at 100% of the total occupant load, with urinals in stalls.

questions.q: Under the UPC, the minimum center-to-center spacing between urinals is:
questions.why: The UPC allows 24 in center to center for urinals; the IPC requires 30 in.

questions.q: Where may a reduced pressure principle backflow preventer NOT be installed?
c: Above grade in a heated room
Below grade in a pit where it could be submerged
On a line under continuous pressure
questions.why: An RPZ can be under continuous pressure but must not be installed below grade where it could flood.

questions.q: A 10 in offset is made with 22-1/2 degree fittings. What is the travel (constant 2.613)?
questions.why: 10 x 2.613 = 26.1 in; 24.1 in is the run.

questions.q: A building drain carries 200 DFU at 1/8 in per ft. Per Table 710.1(1), the minimum size is:
questions.why: A 4 in drain at 1/8 in per ft carries only 180 DFU, so 5 in (390 DFU) is needed.

questions.q: About how much 5.25% bleach gives a 50 ppm dose in 32.6 gallons of water?
questions.why: 32.6 x 50 / 52,500 = 0.031 gal, which is about 4 fluid ounces.

questions.q: A 3 in stack has four branch intervals. Per Table 710.1(2), what is the most DFU it may carry in total?
questions.why: Over three branch intervals a 3 in stack carries 72 DFU, with no more than 20 DFU per interval.

questions.q: Per IPC 2021 Table 917.2, a 3 in single stack under 75 ft tall may carry a maximum of:
questions.why: A 3 in single stack is limited to 24 DFU and is not permitted at 75 ft or taller.

questions.q: What is the minimum vent size for a 4 in drain under IPC 2021 906.2 (vent under 40 ft)?
questions.why: Vents must be at least half the drain diameter, so a 4 in drain needs a 2 in vent.

questions.q: Which hose-threaded outlet is exempt from the vacuum breaker requirement in IPC 2021 608.15.4.2?
c: A laundry sink faucet with hose threads
questions.why: Water heater and boiler drain valves, and clothes washer hose bibbs, are exempt.

questions.q: A 4 in stack carries 320 DFU and needs a 100 ft vent stack. Using Table 906.1 (2-1/2 in = 55 ft, 3 in = 170 ft), the minimum vent size is:
questions.why: 2-1/2 in is good for only 55 ft, so the 3 in vent (170 ft) is the smallest that works.

questions.q: A 15,000 sq ft roof has a 2 in/hr design rainfall. What is the storm flow?
A 1 in indirect waste pipe discharges to a floor sink. The air gap above the flood level rim must be at least:
questions.why: The indirect waste air gap must be at least twice the effective opening: 2 x 1 in = 2 in.

questions.q: A straight horizontal building drain is 230 ft long. How many intermediate cleanouts (beyond the one at the building drain/sewer junction) are needed at 100 ft maximum spacing?
questions.why: Cleanouts may be no more than 100 ft apart, so a 230 ft run needs at least two in between.

questions.q: An indoor arena (A-4) has 3,000 occupants. How many water closets are required for men (1 per 75 for the first 1,500)?
questions.why: Half the load is 1,500 men; 1,500/75 = 20 water closets.

questions.q: An office (Group B) has 300 occupants. How many water closets are required for each sex?
questions.why: 150 per sex: first 50 at 1 per 25 = 2, remaining 100 at 1 per 50 = 2, total 4.

questions.q: A 2,000 sq ft roof receives runoff from a 1,000 sq ft vertical wall. What area is used to size the roof drains?
questions.why: Half the wall area (500 sq ft) is added to the 2,000 sq ft roof.
